title: Branch-scheme criterion and generic spreading for quasi-split nodal fibres
statement:
Let $f:X\to V$ be a flat finitely presented morphism of schemes whose geometric fibres are reduced and pure of dimension one whenever nonempty, and whose nonsmooth geometric points have completed local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ over their algebraically closed residue field $\Omega$. Let $B_f\to D_f$ be the relative branch scheme [def-sfb-nodal-branch-scheme], with $D_f$ the first-Fitting singular subscheme [def-trf-first-fitting-singular-subscheme]. For every $v\in V$, the fibre $X_v$ is quasi-split if and only if, for some integer $n\ge0$, there is an isomorphism of $\kappa(v)$-schemes
$$ (B_f)_v\cong\coprod_{j=1}^{n}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(v). $$
Here quasi-split means that every nonsmooth point of $X_v$ and exactly two normalization points above each such point are rational over $\kappa(v)$ [def-sfb-quasi-split-nodal-fibres]; rational means that the canonical residue-field map is an isomorphism. The assertion includes $n=0$ and smooth or empty fibres.
If, in addition, $f$ is proper and $V$ is Noetherian, then for every integral reduced closed subscheme $T\subseteq V$ with generic point $\xi$ such that $X_\xi$ is quasi-split, there exist a nonempty open subscheme $U\subseteq T$ and an integer $n\ge0$ with an isomorphism of $U$-schemes
$$ B_f\times_V U\cong\coprod_{j=1}^{n} U. $$
In particular every fibre over $U$ is quasi-split. No smoothness or geometric integrality of the generic fibre of $f$ is assumed.

Schemes, flatness, finite presentation, geometric fibres, pure dimension, smoothness, completion, formal power series, normalization, residue fields, spectra, fibre products, properness, integral schemes, closed and open subschemes, and generic points use [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-flat-morphism], [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], [def-weil-geometric-fibre], [def-weil-pure-dimension], [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization], [def-weil-residue-field], [def-weil-affine-spectrum], [def-pc-fibre-product], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-closed-immersion], [def-weil-open-immersion] and [def-sc-generic-point]. Noetherian means locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact.

proof.text: Fix $v$ and put $k=\kappa(v)$, $D=(D_f)_v$, and $B=(B_f)_v$. Apply [lem-sfb-nodal-branch-double-cover]: its flatness and local finite presentation hypotheses follow from those of $f$, and its geometric-node and dimension hypotheses are precisely ours. It identifies $D$ as reduced with points the nonsmooth points of $X_v$, identifies $B$ with $X_v^\nu\times_{X_v}D$, and gives a finite etale degree-two map $B\to D$. Since $f$ is finitely presented, both $D$ and $B$ are finite etale over $k$. By [def-weil-etale-morphism] they are unramified, so [lem-trf-unramified-field-fibre-decomposition] writes them as disjoint unions of spectra of finite separable extensions of $k$. The index sets are finite: a finite scheme over a field is affine with a finite-dimensional coordinate algebra [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], and infinitely many nonzero disjoint summands would give arbitrarily large linearly independent sets.

proof.text: If $X_v$ is quasi-split, [def-sfb-quasi-split-nodal-fibres] says that every nonsmooth point and its two normalization points have residue field $k$. Under the comparison in Step 1 these normalization points are exactly the points of $B$, with the same residue fields, since $D$ is reduced and each of its components is the spectrum of the residue field of its point. Every field summand of the decomposition of $B$ from Step 1 is therefore $k$. Enumerating this finite set gives $B\cong\coprod_{j=1}^{n}\operatorname{Spec}k$. If $D$ is empty so is $B$, giving $n=0$.

source.place: Tag 0CBT (remark-quadratic-extension), Tag 0CBW (lemma-split-node); de Jong, Families of curves and alterations (1997), definition preceding Lemma 5.7 and its first proof paragraph, printed p.615 (publisher scan read online; local PDF WANTED).

proof.text: Conversely suppose $B\cong\coprod_{j=1}^{n}\operatorname{Spec}k$. For any point $d\in D$, the degree-two map of Step 1 has a point $b$ over $d$: its fibre algebra has dimension two over $\kappa(d)$ and hence is nonzero. The structure maps give injective field maps $k\to\kappa(d)\to\kappa(b)=k$ whose composite is the identity under the stated $k$-scheme isomorphism. Thus $\kappa(d)=k$ via its structure map. The fibre over $d$ consists of some of the $k$-components of $B$; its degree is two, so there are exactly two, both rational. Step 1 identifies them with the normalization points over the corresponding nonsmooth point. This is exactly [def-sfb-quasi-split-nodal-fibres]. For $n=0$, degree two forces $D$ empty, and the condition is vacuous. This proves the criterion, including empty and smooth fibres.

proof.text: Now assume properness and the Noetherian hypothesis. The last clause of [lem-sfb-nodal-branch-double-cover] makes $B_f\to V$ finite. Choose an affine open $W=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $V$ containing $\xi$ with $A$ Noetherian, and let $S=T\times_VW$. It is a nonempty affine integral open of $T$ and a closed subscheme of $W$, hence $S=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. The ring $A/I$ is Noetherian because its ideals correspond to ideals of $A$ containing $I$. Put $Z=B_f\times_VS$. Finite morphisms are stable under arbitrary base change by [lem-trf-finite-radicial-basechange], so $Z\to S$ is finite and $Z$ is affine by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. By [pqf-lem-finite-fp-locnoeth], $Z\to S$ is of finite presentation. Steps 1-3 at $\xi$ give an integer $n\ge0$ and an isomorphism $Z_\xi\cong\coprod_{j=1}^{n}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\xi)$.

Let $Y=\coprod_{j=1}^{n}S$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-affine-coproduct-spectrum] it is $\operatorname{Spec}((A/I)^n)$ with its diagonal structure map to $S$. This algebra is a finite $A/I$-module, generated by its $n$ coordinate vectors, also for $n=0$ when it is the zero ring. Thus $Y\to S$ is finite by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and is of finite presentation by [pqf-lem-finite-fp-locnoeth]. Its generic fibre is $\coprod_{j=1}^{n}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\xi)$, since tensoring a finite product of modules with the fraction field gives the corresponding finite product. Apply [lem-sbc-generic-fibre-iso-spread-base-open] to the affine $S$-schemes $Z,Y$ and their generic isomorphism: $S$ is integral, and both structure maps are locally finitely presented by Step 4 and this step. It supplies an open $U\subseteq S$ containing $\xi$ and $Z|_U\cong Y|_U=\coprod_{j=1}^{n}U$. This $U$ is a nonempty open of $T$.

source.place: Tag 01ZM, lemma-descend-finite-presentation, (2)-(3), as encapsulated by lem-sbc-generic-fibre-iso-spread-base-open; finite affine coproduct: Schemes Tag 01I5 (lemma-disjoint-union-affines).

proof.text: For each $u\in U$, base change of the resulting isomorphism to $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)$ gives $(B_f)_u\cong\coprod_{j=1}^{n}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)$. The criterion already proved in Steps 1-3 for the original $f$ at the image of $u$ applies, because an open subscheme of the closed subscheme $T\subseteq V$ has the same residue fields as $V$ at its points. Hence every $X_u$ is quasi-split. When $n=0$ the isomorphism says that the branch scheme is empty throughout $U$, so all these fibres are smooth or empty by Step 1. No hypothesis on smoothness or geometric integrality of $X_\xi$ was used.

Small cases tested: empty or smooth fibre (n=0), split node, non-split node x²−ay², node at a non-rational point, smoothing xy=t.
